batch: BitLocker drive-type policy and default-profile source recheck

findings.policyChoices: Microsoft documents AES-CBC 128/256 and XTS-AES 128/256 for operating-system, fixed-data and removable-data drives. It recommends XTS-AES and says the 128/256-bit choice depends on device performance.
findings.effectiveDefault: When the policy is not configured, new BitLocker encryption defaults to XTS-AES 128-bit.
findings.activationBoundary: The policy is enforced when encryption starts. Changing policy does not restart encryption or change an already-encrypted drive.
findings.hardwareEncryption: The policy does not apply to hardware-based encryption; the drive's hardware algorithm is set when partitioned.
findings.cspContract: The BitLocker CSP EncryptionMethodByDriveType node is device-scoped and Microsoft says all three drive-type values must be sent together in one SyncML request. RIDE's candidates write local Group Policy registry values and do not configure CSP/MDM.

catalogAndProfileReview.registryHandlerScope: Each operation writes only its local Group Policy DWORD, does not write CSP/MDM settings and does not encrypt/decrypt or modify volume protectors.
catalogAndProfileReview.candidateSupport: Windows 11 candidate only; SupportedTargets remains empty pending disposable-target policy precedence, observation and exact saved-state acceptance.

operatorGuidanceChange: Explain that the profile chooses XTS-AES 256-bit as a user-approved security default, while Microsoft's guidance makes key length a device-performance choice; users may select 128-bit through the declared setting state when performance is more important.

deferred: Windows 11 native policy precedence/readback and exact saved-state restore remain pending because VM access is blocked before checkpoint inspection.

estimates.adjustment: None; source recheck closes no legacy outcome and changes no catalog/profile state.
